# --description--

Calling `split("")` with an empty separator turns a string into an array of its single characters.
Arrays have a `reverse()` method, so you can reverse a string by splitting, reversing and joining:
```javascript
let word = "abc";
console.log(word.split("").reverse().join(""));
// prints cba
```

# --instructions--

Write a function `isPalindrome(word)` that returns `true` when `word` reads the same backwards, ignoring letter case

# --asserts--

`isPalindrome("racecar")` must return `true`.

```javascript

```

`isPalindrome("Level")` must return `true`.

```javascript

```

`isPalindrome("hello")` must return `false`.


# --solutions--

```javascript
function isPalindrome(word) {
  let lower = word.toLowerCase();
  return lower === lower.split("").reverse().join("");
}
```
